messages:
alex_support: FYI — customer on our hosted API reporting intermittent streaming failures for Safari users. They see partial output, then the EventSource connection silently drops and doesn't reconnect. Customer says it happens behind a CDN (Cloudflare) and only for Safari on iOS and macOS. They attached network logs. Escalating for triage.

mika_dev: thanks — can you paste the raw request/response headers and a minimal repro? need to know if Authorization header is present on the open request and if any 304s/304-related caching shows up. safari-specific bugs often surface when an edge returns 304 instead of 200 for chunked SSE.

alex_support: here are snippets from the customer's HAR and our edge logs (redacted):

- Client: Safari 15.6 / iOS 15.6
- Endpoint: GET https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-medium
- Request headers they show: Accept: text/event-stream, Cache-Control: no-cache, Authorization: Bearer <token>

Edge log (Cloudflare worker):
```
{ method: GET, url: /v1/stream?model=redwood-medium, status: 304, served_from_cache: true, cf_cache_status: HIT }
```

Customer network console: EventSource connected then after ~8s the lastEventId stops updating; console shows: "EventSource failed to connect" and no reconnect attempts.

sam_frontend: this screams the classic Safari+304 SSE stall. Safari will treat 304 responses differently for EventSource and may stop feeding the stream if the edge returns a conditional 304 instead of a fresh 200 with chunked body. Also some CDNs will convert a 200+chunked incremental into a 304 when they believe the resource is fresh. For SSE we need a streaming 200 with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and no intermediate 304s.

mika_dev: also check the reconnect auth path. EventSource in browsers can't add Authorization header for reconnects if the underlying browser drops it or the token expires mid-stream — some customers have polyfills that rewrite reconnection logic but that can leave stale tokens. Does the customer show any 401s right after the disconnect?

alex_support: they do. In the timeline there's a 401 on POST /v1/retry-auth and an immediate abort on the SSE. They say their frontend tries to re-open the EventSource but the new handshake gets a 401 until they refresh the page (which reloads a new token).

jordan_sre: pulled the edge trace for that timeframe — we have repeated conditional requests where the origin returned 200 initially, then the edge served subsequent requests as 304 from cache. Example:
```
edge -> origin: If-None-Match: "etag-abc"
origin -> edge: 200 (streaming chunked)
edge caches response
later edge -> origin: If-None-Match: "etag-abc"
origin -> edge: 304
edge -> client: 304
```
Safari treats that 304 path poorly for EventSource. On top of that, Cloudflare removed the Authorization header when serving from cache because of our worker config. So the reconnection path sometimes arrives at edge with no Authorization, which yields a 401 to the origin if the edge does contact the origin.

sam_frontend: repro steps I used locally (Safari desktop) — quick paste:
```
// minimal repro in console
let es = new EventSource('https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=toy&no_cache=1');
es.onmessage = e => console.log('msg', e.data);
es.onerror = e => console.log('es error', e);
```
I toggled Cloudflare dev mode off/on and saw the difference: when the edge responded with 200 and Transfer-Encoding: chunked, stream flows. When edge returned 304 / cached response, the browser receives a terminal event and doesn't process further chunks.

mika_dev: thanks. Two vectors to act on: 1) immediate customer workaround, 2) infra/product changes. For workaround: advise the customer to add a short cache-busting query (e.g., ?no_cache=TIMESTAMP) or use a short-lived signed token in query string so edge won't serve cached 304. Also recommend switching to XHR+ReadableStream or WebSocket for Safari users if feasible. 

alex_support: noted, shared these two options with the customer. they asked for a secure recommended fix — they don't want tokens in querystrings long-term.

jordan_sre: infra side — we should ensure our streaming endpoints are never cached at the edge. Proposed quick rule: Cloudflare route /v1/stream* to bypass cache (Cache-Control: no-store) and ensure edge returns 200 from origin for each client (disable ETag/If-None-Match for that route). Also ensure the worker preserves Authorization on reconnects (Vary: Authorization) or simply drop caching on that route entirely. I'll open a ticket.

deploy_bot: deploy queued: CF rule update (bypass cache) -> PR 5123, rolling to staging in ~15m, prod next day pending sign-off.

sam_frontend: small note: some customers used polyfills (event-source-polyfill) that reimplement reconnect by creating a new XHR with Authorization header preserved. That helps with token rotation but doesn't fix the 304 streaming stall. Also Safari's implementation is aggressive about caching for event-streams with 304s. So server-side no-cache is the real fix.

mika_dev: for server behavior, we should also ensure SSE responses include these headers:
```
Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, private
Connection: keep-alive
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
X-Accel-Buffering: no   # for some proxies (nginx)
```
And avoid setting ETag for the streaming resource. Confirming these should stop conditional 304 responses.

alex_support: customer confirmed they can roll a quick client change (no_cache query param) while we push infra fix. They want a written repro for their security folks. I prepared a minimal reproducible HAR and the short repro steps above.

jordan_sre: created ticket INFRA-2147 to add CDN bypass for /v1/stream and to strip ETag on stream responses. Assigned to infra; ETA 48h. Also adding a monitoring alert for SSE error rate > 2% for Safari user agents.

mika_dev: I'll add a short doc to devex explaining recommended headers and a note about Safari+304. We should also update our client SDKs to emit a clear error when EventSource reconnects repeatedly with 401 so apps can re-auth before a full page reload.

alex_support: customer happy for now with workaround. keeping thread open until INFRA-2147 closes and PR 5123 deploys to prod. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sam_frontend: FYI — added a short snippet for customers showing secure reconnect pattern using a short-lived signed URL TTL=60s (rotate on server), plus fallback to fetch+stream for Safari. Paste if needed.

mika_dev: nice. Can you attach that snippet to the infra ticket and the devex doc?

jordan_sre: done. closing loop when PR 5123 is live.

alex_support: closing note — lessons: avoid caching SSE endpoints, don't rely on 304 for streaming, handle auth rotation on reconnects. I'll update the support KB with reproduction steps and mitigation.
